# Fixture provenance and licensing

Every file in this directory MUST have an entry here. CI enforces this
(`tools/check-fixture-licenses.sh`): an unlisted spec fails the build, as
does any tracked testdata containing a known-proprietary marker.

| File | Source | License basis for redistribution |
|------|--------|----------------------------------|
| `paystack.json` / `paystack.yaml` | https://github.com/PaystackHQ/openapi (dist/paystack.yaml; JSON is our deterministic conversion) | MIT — repo `LICENSE`, "Copyright (c) 2022 PaystackOSS". Notice reproduced below. |
| `stripe.trimmed.json` | https://github.com/stripe/openapi (spec3.json, deterministically trimmed to 25 paths + component closure) | MIT — repo `LICENSE`, "Copyright (c) 2011- Stripe, Inc." Notice reproduced below. |
| `appveyor-swagger.json` | https://github.com/kevinoid/appveyor-swagger (swagger.yaml at repo root), retrieved through the APIs.guru mirror at https://api.apis.guru/v2/specs/appveyor.com/1.0.0/swagger.json | MIT — kevinoid/appveyor-swagger `LICENSE.txt`, "Copyright 2016 Kevin Locke". Notice reproduced below. See the note on this file. |
| `synthetic-sms.swagger2.json` | Generated by `tools/gen-synthetic-fixtures.py` | Invented; Apache-2.0 (this repo) |
| `synthetic-payments.postman.json` | Generated by `tools/gen-synthetic-fixtures.py` | Invented; Apache-2.0 (this repo) |

## Note on `appveyor-swagger.json`

This file is an **unofficial** community-maintained Swagger description of the
AppVeyor REST API, written by Kevin Locke and licensed MIT. It is not published
by AppVeyor. Two things follow:

* The redistribution grant is Kevin Locke's MIT license, not anything from
  AppVeyor and not APIs.guru's CC0. APIs.guru's CC0 dedication covers its own
  directory metadata; it does not and cannot relicense the third-party
  descriptions it aggregates, so "obtained from APIs.guru" is not a grant.
* The spec's own `info.license` field says "AppVeyor End User License Agreement
  (EULA)" and `info.termsOfService` points at AppVeyor's terms. Those describe
  the *AppVeyor service* the API belongs to, not this document. Do not read
  that embedded field as the license of the file.

The copy here came through the APIs.guru mirror, so it carries APIs.guru's
added `x-apisguru-categories`, `x-logo` and `x-origin` annotations on top of
the upstream document; `x-origin` records the kevinoid source URL.

Contact addresses appearing inside these fixtures (`techsupport@paystack.com`,
`dev-platform@stripe.com`, `team@appveyor.com`, `nuget@appveyor.com`) and the
example payload addresses in the Paystack spec are upstream-published content
carried verbatim from the MIT-licensed sources above. They are not customer
data and must not be edited: these files are byte-pinned by committed parity
goldens.

Rules for adding a fixture:

1. **No provider content without an explicit license grant.** "Publicly
   fetchable" is not a grant. Postman Documenter pages, docs-site prose, and
   specs marked private are all off-limits regardless of reachability.
2. When a test needs a real-world *shape* you cannot license, generate a
   synthetic fixture with the same structural properties (see
   `tools/gen-synthetic-fixtures.py`) and name it `synthetic-*`.
3. Add the entry here in the same commit as the file.
